prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline. Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Business Rules Registry governs fairness/spacing/subscriptions/runway-queue thresholds/protected-flights. Cedarbell normalizes Airport Capacity Plan;Marlinstone predicts demand;Capacity Assessment Module compares Airport Acceptance Rate/runway/taxiway/sector limits. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;runway/fix/Ground Delay Program constraints;capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Halcyon confirms publication,requests delay/fairness adjustments,checks Slot Compliance State. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:advisory movements/timestamped milestones. Quartzline→Blueharbor:Stand Tow Request Form,recalculation. Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities;Lantern distributes approvals. Saffron shall confirm revisions before freeze-horizon;justified connection/crew/rotation reviews. Quartzline verifies queue-card pad-entry order before staging authorization;must coordinate every pad release with Brindle. Emberline withholds push clearances above safe holding capacity until below configured threshold. Ironleaf reserves positions only with achievable pad-release time/valid runway taxi path. Foxglove records fluid

New part:
S411: If conditions improve, the Regional Flow Manager may approve a staged landing-rate increase, but the increase is limited until the Tower Sequence Manager confirms stable spacing and runway occupancy performance.
S412: Diversion triggers are monitored continuously and include predicted holding beyond operator fuel thresholds, loss of required approach capability, sustained sector saturation, and runway availability below the minimum safe acceptance rate.
S413: The Network Operations Liaison coordinates with affected airline control centers when diversion risk becomes material so that alternate airport decisions can be made before fuel margins become critical.
S414: The Emergency Response Coordinator is informed when a diversion trigger is associated with an aircraft condition that could affect rescue and firefighting readiness at Meridian or at an alternate airport.
S415: During Adverse Weather Mode, tactical adjustments are reviewed more frequently because landing-rate stability may depend on short-lived runway configuration and approach spacing opportunities.
S416: During Capacity Reduction State, the Regional Flow Manager may combine arrival regulation with departure metering to protect surface balance and prevent inbound aircraft from occupying gates needed for recovery flights.
S417: All rate changes, rejected options, coordination outcomes, and effective times are written to the Audit Event Ledger for later review.
S418: The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses the recorded regulation history to compare predicted holding, actual airborne delay, diversion outcomes, and achieved landing rates for continuous improvement of Meridian arrival management.
S419: The Integrated Tactical Management Position is the primary workstation for real-time coordination of Meridian departure flow, arrival flow, airport capacity, and airspace constraints.
S420: It presents a combined tactical view so that the Regional Flow Manager can compare planned demand, measured throughput, and active control measures without changing applications.
S421: The Common Situation Display provides the base map, timeline, flight list, and measure status panels used at the position.
S422: The Regional Flow Platform synchronizes the tactical display with the Time Synchronization Service so that all timestamps, countdowns, and validity intervals use the same operational clock.
S423: The Arrival Regulation Console is also known as Nightjar at the Integrated Tactical Management Position, where the alias is displayed only in operator profile help text.
S424: Arrival demand is monitored against the Airport Acceptance Rate, current sequencing performance, and any Ground Delay Program that remains in effect.
S425: The Tower Supervisor uses the display to see runway assignment pressure, airborne sequence spacing, and expected crossing points at the North Runway Meter and the South Runway Meter.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
